question: Y9
shape: EU energy labelling / repeal of Delegated Regulation 874/2012
answer:
# Compliance note — repeal of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012

## 0. Question and short answer

**Question.** For Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2015, as in force on 21 November 2026: (a) when was Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 repealed, and (b) which two specified paragraphs were repealed earlier, on 25 December 2019?

**Answer (a).** Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 was repealed **with effect from 1 September 2021**.

**Answer (b).** The two paragraphs repealed earlier, with effect from **25 December 2019**, were **paragraph 2 of Article 3** and **paragraph 2 of Article 4** of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012.

**Title correction (carried into all citations below).** The instrument is Commission **Delegated** Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019, adopted under Article 11(5) and Article 16(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 — not a "Commission Regulation". Its official short form is "Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015".

---

## 1. Version pinning — what "as in force on 2026-11-21" resolves to

The constraint in ask 1 requires that the answer be read off the text in force on 21 November 2026, not the original 2019 text.

Consolidation history listed on the EUR-Lex act page:

| Consolidated version date | Basis |
|---|---|
| 05/12/2019 | initial legal act, OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, pp. 68–101 |
| 01/03/2021 | after M1 |
| 01/05/2021 | after M1 |
| 01/07/2021 | after M1 |
| 01/09/2021 | after M1 |
| **30/09/2023** | **after M2 — current consolidated version** |

Amending acts recorded in the consolidation header:

- **M1** — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/340 of 17 December 2020, OJ L 68, 26.2.2021, p. 62.
- **M2** — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2048 of 4 July 2023, OJ L 236, 26.9.2023, p. 1.

The EUR-Lex act page, as served on 23 November 2026, states "In force — This act has been changed. Current consolidated version: 30/09/2023" and gives the dated ELI `http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/2015/2023-09-30`. No consolidated version later than 30 September 2023 is listed. **Accordingly, the text in force on 21 November 2026 is the consolidated text of 30 September 2023** (original text as amended by M1 and M2), and that is the text relied on here.

**Materiality of the amendments to this question: nil.** In the 30/09/2023 consolidation, Article 9 sits under a `▼B` marker, i.e. it is base-text wording and has not been replaced by M1 or M2. M1's textual insertion is in Article 10 (second paragraph: "…and point 2(a) of Article 3 shall apply from 1 March 2022") and in the Annexes; M2 amends the Annexes. Neither amending act touches Article 9. The repeal dates are therefore identical in the original 2019 text, in the 30/09/2023 consolidation, and in any version in between.

---

## 2. Operative provision — Article 9 (Repeal), verbatim

> **Article 9 — Repeal**
>
> Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, with the exception of paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 which are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019.

For completeness, the adjacent provisions that fix the calendar:

> **Article 10 — Entry into force and application**
>
> This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
>
> It shall apply from 1 September 2021. However, point 1(b) of Article 3 shall apply from 1 May 2021, and point 2(a) of Article 3 shall apply from 1 March 2022. *(the final clause added by M1)*

---

## 3. Decomposition of the answer

The single sentence in Article 9 creates **two distinct repeal events**:

| Event | Date | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Partial repeal (earlier) | **25 December 2019** | Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) of Del. Reg. (EU) No 874/2012 only |
| Principal repeal | **1 September 2021** | The remainder of Del. Reg. (EU) No 874/2012 (all provisions other than Art. 3(2) and Art. 4(2)) |

So the answer to (a) is **1 September 2021**, and the answer to (b) is **Article 3(2) and Article 4(2)** of the repealed delegated regulation. A file that records "874/2012 was repealed on 25 December 2019" is wrong: on that date only the two named paragraphs fell; the rest of the regulation remained in force for a further twenty months.

---

## 4. Verification performed

1. **Internal arithmetic.** OJ publication date 5 December 2019; Article 10 first paragraph sets entry into force on the twentieth day following publication → 25 December 2019. That is precisely the date Article 9 assigns to the earlier partial repeal of Art. 3(2) and Art. 4(2). The two provisions are mutually consistent; no date has been mis-transcribed.
2. **Date alignment with application.** The principal repeal date in Article 9 (1 September 2021) coincides with the application date in Article 10 (1 September 2021), as the act intends. The two earlier application dates in Article 10 (1 May 2021 for point 1(b) of Article 3; 1 March 2022 for point 2(a) of Article 3, added by M1) do not disturb Article 9.
3. **Source triangulation.** Article 9 reads identically, word for word, in: the EUR-Lex OJ HTML rendering (`uriserv:OJ.L_.2019.315.01.0068.01.ENG`); the EUR-Lex ELI page (`eli/reg_del/2019/2015/oj/eng`) and the 30/09/2023 consolidated page; the legislation.gov.uk plain-text Article 9 view (both the 2019-03-11 and the 2020-12-31 point-in-time versions); the legislation.gov.uk adopted-text PDF; and the Welsh-language view. No textual variant exists to resolve.
4. **Amendment check.** Article 9 carries `▼B` in the consolidation, confirming it was not amended by M1 or M2 (see §1).
5. **Authenticity caveat.** The EUR-Lex consolidation carries the standard disclaimer that only the text published in the Official Journal is authentic. Operative wording was therefore verified against the OJ-published text (OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68), and the consolidation was used only to confirm that Article 9 has not since been amended.

**Residual risk.** The answer would change only if an amendment to Article 9 entered into force between 30 September 2023 and 21 November 2026. None is recorded: the EUR-Lex act page served on 23 November 2026 still lists 30/09/2023 as the current consolidated version, and Article 9's subject matter (a spent repeal) is not a plausible target for amendment.

---

## 5. Citation block (ready to paste into a compliance file)

- **Act relied on:** Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to energy labelling of light sources and repealing Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 (Text with EEA relevance). OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68–101. C/2019/1805. ELI: `http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/2015/oj`. CELEX: 32019R2015.
- **Version relied on:** consolidated text of 30 September 2023 (as amended by Del. Reg. (EU) 2021/340, OJ L 68, 26.2.2021, p. 62, and Del. Reg. (EU) 2023/2048, OJ L 236, 26.9.2023, p. 1). ELI: `http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/2015/2023-09-30`.
- **Provision:** Article 9 (Repeal), read with Article 10 (Entry into force and application).
- **Act repealed:** Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 — *OJ reference not verified from the sources consulted for this note; confirm against EUR-Lex before citing in a filed document.*

---

## 6. Practical consequences to record in the file

- Any obligation sourced from **Article 3(2) or Article 4(2) of Del. Reg. (EU) No 874/2012** ended on **25 December 2019**; documentation must not rely on those paragraphs for any period after that date.
- Any obligation sourced from **any other provision of Del. Reg. (EU) No 874/2012** remained live until **31 August 2021** and ended on **1 September 2021**.
- From **1 September 2021** the governing labelling instrument for light sources is Del. Reg. (EU) 2019/2015 as amended (M1, M2), not 874/2012.

question: Y13
shape: EU finance / find the right rule
answer:
MEMORANDUM — Scope of the EU prospectus regime for a sub-EUR 1 000 000 Union offer, as in force on 21 November 2026

I. QUESTION PRESENTED
For an offer of securities to the public in the Union with total consideration below EUR 1 000 000, calculated over 12 months: (a) does the EU prospectus regulation apply on 2026-11-21, and (b) what is the applicable threshold?

II. SHORT ANSWER
(a) VERDICT — No. No prospectus is required. The offer falls within the small-offer exemption, which in the text in force is located in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 (the Prospectus Regulation) as amended: offers of securities to the public are exempted from the Article 3(1) prospectus obligation where the total aggregated consideration in the Union for the securities offered is below the applicable ceiling. EUR 1 000 000 is below every threshold that can apply on 2026-11-21 — the EUR 12 000 000 ceiling and the EUR 5 000 000 Member State alternative.

(b) VALUE — The threshold is EUR 12 000 000, per issuer or offeror, calculated over 12 months (Article 3(2), point (b)). By way of derogation, a Member State may apply an exemption threshold of EUR 5 000 000 (Article 3(2a)) and must notify the Commission and ESMA of the amount it applies (Article 3(2b)). Because the offer is below EUR 1 000 000, the answer is identical under either figure.

III. TEXT RELIED ON (version in force)
1. Article 3(2) (ESMA Interactive Single Rulebook, Prospectus Regulation, Article 3 — fetched 2026-11-23; EUR-Lex consolidated version ELI reg/2017/1129/2026-06-05):
   "Without prejudice to Article 4, offers of securities to the public shall be exempted from the obligation to publish a prospectus set out in paragraph 1 provided that: (a) such offers are not subject to notification in accordance with Article 25; (b) the total aggregated consideration in the Union for the securities offered is less than EUR 12 000 000 per issuer or offeror calculated over a period of 12 months. Member States shall notify the Commission and ESMA whether and how they decide to apply the exemption pursuant to the first subparagraph, including the monetary amount below which the exemption for offers in that Member State applies."
2. Article 3(2a): "By way of derogation from paragraph 2, point (b), Member States may exempt offers of securities to the public from the obligation to publish a prospectus set out in paragraph 1 provided that the total aggregated consideration in the Union for the securities offered is less than EUR 5 000 000 per issuer or offeror calculated over a period of 12 months."
3. Article 3(2b): Member States must notify the Commission and ESMA where they adopt the EUR 5 000 000 threshold, and where they subsequently adopt instead the EUR 12 000 000 threshold.
4. Article 3(2c) (aggregation): "The total aggregated consideration ... shall take into account the total aggregated consideration of all ongoing offers of securities to the public and offers of securities to the public made within the 12 months preceding the start date of a new offer of securities to the public, except for those offers ... for which a prospectus was published or that were subject to any exemption from the obligation to publish a prospectus pursuant to Article 1(4), first subparagraph. Moreover, the total aggregated consideration of the securities offered to the public shall include all types and classes of securities offered."
5. Article 3(2d): where an offer is exempted under Article 3(2)(b) or 3(2a), a Member State may nevertheless require the issuer to file and make public a document containing the information in Article 7(3)-(10) and (12), or a national-equivalent document of no greater extent.
6. Article 3(3): "Without prejudice to Article 1(5), securities shall only be admitted to trading on a regulated market situated or operating within the Union after prior publication of a prospectus in accordance with this Regulation."

IV. ANALYSIS

1. Instrument and version. "EU prospectus regulation" = Regulation (EU) 2017/1129. The version applicable on 2026-11-21 is the consolidation dated 5 June 2026 (EUR-Lex ELI .../reg/2017/1129/2026-06-05), which is the latest consolidation preceding the target date and whose Article 3 text matches the ESMA Interactive Single Rulebook display captured on 23 November 2026. That text is the post-Listing Act architecture: the small-offer exemption is expressed as an exemption from the Article 3(1) prospectus obligation (Article 3(2)-(2d)) rather than as a carve-out from the Regulation's scope, and the monetary ceiling is EUR 12 000 000 with a EUR 5 000 000 Member State alternative. (The EUR 5 000 000 / EUR 8 000 000 figures referred to in earlier analysis as "pending reforms" are superseded; the operative figures in the text in force are EUR 12 000 000 and EUR 5 000 000.)

2. Application to the facts. Total consideration below EUR 1 000 000 < EUR 12 000 000 and < EUR 5 000 000. Accordingly the offer is exempted from the obligation to publish a prospectus under Article 3(1), irrespective of which threshold the relevant Member State has notified. Two conditions must be checked and, on the assumed facts, are satisfied: (i) the offer is not one "subject to notification in accordance with Article 25" (Article 3(2)(a)); and (ii) it is not an offer for which the exemption is disapplied at national level — the mechanism in Article 3(2), second subparagraph, contemplates Member States notifying "whether and how" they apply the exemption, so the notification position of the Member State(s) of the offer must be confirmed (see V below).

3. Aggregation over 12 months (Article 3(2c)) — how the threshold is measured. The figure is not per-offer. It is: (i) measured "in the Union" (offers outside the Union do not count; offers across Member States do); (ii) per issuer or offeror; (iii) the sum of all ongoing offers plus all offers made in the 12 months preceding the start date of the new offer; (iv) across all types and classes of securities; and (v) excluding offers for which a prospectus was published and offers exempt under Article 1(4), first subparagraph (qualified investors, fewer than 150 non-qualified investors, EUR 100 000 denomination per unit, EUR 100 000 per investor, etc.). Offers previously made in reliance on the Article 3(2)/3(2a) exemption are NOT excluded, which is the anti-splitting rule: successive exempt offers aggregate.
   Worked example: issuer made an exempt offer of EUR 600 000 in March 2026 (no prospectus, not an Article 1(4) offer) and proposes a further EUR 500 000 offer in December 2026. Aggregated: 600 000 + 500 000 = EUR 1 100 000 < EUR 12 000 000 (and < EUR 5 000 000) — still exempt. (Note: EUR 1 100 000 would have exceeded the pre-reform EUR 1 000 000 figure, which is precisely the change the amendment effects; the example is not a statement about the pre-reform regime.)

4. What the exemption does and does not do.
   - It disapplies the Article 3(1) prospectus obligation for the offer. It does not disapply Article 3(3): admission to trading of the securities on a regulated market still requires a prior prospectus unless an Article 1(5) exemption applies (e.g. fungible securities representing less than 20% over 12 months, or a class already admitted on another regulated market for more than 18 months).
   - It does not prevent national requirements: Article 3(2d) permits a Member State to require a filing of an Article 7(3)-(10) and (12) document, or a national-equivalent document.
   - It does not displace Regulation (EU) 596/2014 (market abuse), Directive 2014/65/EU (MiFID II) conduct and product-governance rules, or national private-placement, advertising and consumer-protection rules.
   - A voluntary prospectus may still be drawn up under Article 4, in which case the Regulation applies to that prospectus in full.
   - Offers that independently satisfy an Article 1(4) exemption (qualified investors, fewer than 150 non-qualified persons, EUR 100 000 denomination, EUR 100 000 per investor) are outside the Article 3(1) obligation on that separate ground and are excluded from the Article 3(2c) aggregation.

5. Robustness. Even on the pre-amendment text (Article 1(3): "this Regulation shall not apply to an offer of securities to the public with a total consideration in the Union of less than EUR 1 000 000, calculated over a period of 12 months"), the verdict for a sub-EUR 1 000 000 offer would be the same: no prospectus. The verdict therefore does not depend on the version question; only the stated threshold figure does.

V. VERIFICATION POINTS BEFORE RELIANCE (each is a confirmatory step, not an open question of substance)
1. Version check: confirm on EUR-Lex "all consolidated versions" of 2017/1129 that the version applicable on 2026-11-21 is the 5 June 2026 consolidation, and confirm in the amending act (Listing Act package, Regulation (EU) 2024/2809) the application date of the Article 3 amendments. If — contrary to the sources relied on — the pre-amendment text were still applicable on that date, the verdict in III/IV is unchanged and the threshold would be EUR 1 000 000 with a Member State option up to EUR 8 000 000; that alternative is flagged, not asserted.
2. Member State notifications under Article 3(2b): confirm the amount notified by the Member State(s) in which the offer is made (EUR 12 000 000 or EUR 5 000 000). Immaterial here: EUR 1 000 000 is below both.
3. Article 3(2)(a): confirm the offer is not one "subject to notification in accordance with Article 25" of the Regulation.
4. Status of Article 1(3): confirm whether the original EUR 1 000 000 scope carve-out subsists in the 2026 consolidation (the ESMA display places the small-offer regime in Article 3, which suggests it has been superseded). Immaterial to the verdict: the offer is exempt either way.

VI. RESULT
Ask 2 (verdict): No — no prospectus is required; the offer is exempt under Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 as in force on 2026-11-21.
Ask 3 (value): EUR 12 000 000 — Article 3(2), point (b), per issuer or offeror over 12 months in the Union; Member States may instead apply EUR 5 000 000 under Article 3(2a).
cautions: The recompute vote did not run, so no figure in this answer was recomputed.
The answer gives 1.2e+07 EUR for ask 3, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.

question: Y9
shape: EU energy labelling / repeal of Delegated Regulation 874/2012
answer:
REGULATORY DETERMINATION — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 (energy labelling of light sources); temporal frame: as in force on 21 November 2026.

1. TEMPORAL FRAME (ask 1 — constraint, not a value).
The act is Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 with regard to energy labelling of light sources and repealing Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 (OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68; CELEX 32019R2015; ELI http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2019/2015/oj). EUR-Lex records 'Date of end of validity: No end date' and, as retrieved on 23 November 2026 (two days after the reference date), lists the current consolidated version as 30/09/2023 (ELI .../reg_del/2019/2015/2023-09-30). The consolidation history shows exactly two amendments: M1 = Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/340 (OJ L 68, 26.2.2021, p. 62) and M2 = Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2048 (OJ L 236, 26.9.2023, p. 1). Accordingly, the version in force on 2026-11-21 is the 30/09/2023 consolidated text. In that consolidated text, Article 9 is reproduced under the '▼B' marker, i.e. as originally adopted and untouched by M1 and M2 (M1's only footprint in the end matter is the added application date in Article 10, second paragraph: '...and point 2(a) of Article 3 shall apply from 1 March 2022'). The repeal provision is therefore stable across the 2019 original, the 2021 and 2023 consolidations, and the text in force on 2026-11-21.

2. OPERATIVE PROVISION — Article 9 (Repeal) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015, verbatim:
'Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, with the exception of paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 which are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019.'
The same wording is returned by three independent renderings: the OJ PDF (CELEX:32019R2015), the EUR-Lex 'ALL' page, and the legislation.gov.uk reproduction (Article 9, U.K. rendering).

3. ANSWER TO ASK 2 — date of repeal of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012:
1 September 2021 (2021-09-01).
This is the date from which the repeal of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 takes effect, subject only to the two-paragraph carve-out in section 4. It is a 'repeal with effect from' date, not the date of adoption (11.3.2019), not the date of publication (5.12.2019) and not the date of entry into force (25.12.2019).

4. ANSWER TO ASK 3 — the two paragraphs repealed earlier, on 25 December 2019:
paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012, i.e. Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) of that Delegated Regulation.
These are carved out of the general repeal and repealed with effect from 25 December 2019, i.e. 20 months and 7 days before the remainder. Read precisely: the subject of both repeal dates is Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012; the paragraphs are paragraphs of that instrument, not of Regulation (EU) 2019/2015.

5. CORROBORATION (independent of Article 9's wording).
(a) The EUR-Lex document-relationship table for 32019R2015 lists, under 'Repeal': '32012R0874 — Partial repeal — 25/12/2019' and '32012R0874 — Repeal — 01/09/2021'. Two rows, two dates, matching Article 9 exactly.
(b) The EUR-Lex 'Dates' block for 32019R2015 gives: Date of document 11/03/2019 (adoption); Date of effect 25/12/2019 — Entry into force ('Date pub. +20, See Art 10'); Date of effect 01/05/2021 — Application (partial, Art 10); Date of effect 01/09/2021 — Application (Art 10); Date of effect 01/03/2022 — Application (partial, Art 10); Deadline 25/12/2024 — Review (Art 8); Date of end of validity — no end date. The 25/12/2019 date is arithmetically confirmed: OJ publication 5.12.2019 + 20 days = 25.12.2019, so the early partial repeal of Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) of 874/2012 coincides with the entry into force of 2019/2015, while the main repeal coincides with the date of application (1.9.2021).
(c) The EUR-Lex consolidation of the repealed act (CELEX 02012R0874-20210901) carries the header 'Repealed by: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019, OJ L 315, 68, 5.12.2019', and shows consolidated versions dated 25/12/2019, 09/08/2020 and 01/09/2021 — the 25/12/2019 version being the consolidation generated by the early partial repeal.

6. READING RULES APPLIED (stated so the determination can be audited).
- 'Repealed' = formal repeal by a legal act (Article 9 of 2019/2015), not expiry, not supersession in substance.
- Entry into force (25.12.2019), application (1.9.2021; with 1.5.2021 for Article 3(1)(b) and 1.3.2022 for Article 3(2)(a), per M1) and repeal (25.12.2019 in part; 1.9.2021 in remainder) are kept distinct; the question is answered on the repeal axis only.
- Dates are taken as written in the instrument (European convention, DD/MM/YYYY): '1 September 2021' and '25 December 2019'; no recalculation beyond the publication + 20 days entry-into-force check in 5(b).
- The 2021/340 and 2023/2048 amendments do not alter Article 9, so the answer is invariant across the 2019 original and the version in force on 2026-11-21.

7. CAVEATS / LIMITS OF THIS DETERMINATION.
- The consolidation retrieved is 30/09/2023, which is the current one as of the 23.11.2026 retrieval; no later amendment exists in the record. If a further amendment after 30.09.2023 were adopted and published, it would have to be checked against Article 9 — nothing in the retrieved record suggests one.
- EUR-Lex consolidations are documentation tools without legal effect; the authentic text is the OJ version (OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68). Here the OJ PDF and the consolidation agree verbatim on Article 9, so the point is academic.
- The substantive content of Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is not reproduced in the retrieved passages and is therefore not asserted here; the answer identifies the paragraphs by number only, which is what the question asks.

8. BOTTOM LINE.
Under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 as in force on 21 November 2026 (consolidated text of 30/09/2023), Article 9 provides that Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, except that paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 were repealed earlier, with effect from 25 December 2019.

question: Y13
shape: EU finance / find the right rule
answer:
LEGAL OPINION - Application of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 to an offer of securities to the public in the Union with total consideration below EUR 1 000 000, as in force on 21 November 2026

A. BOTTOM LINE

1. Verdict (ask 2): NO. The EU prospectus regulation - Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 - does not apply. Article 1(3), first subparagraph, provides that 'this Regulation shall not apply to an offer of securities to the public with a total consideration in the Union of less than EUR 1 000 000, which shall be calculated over a period of 12 months.' This is a disapplication of the Regulation, not merely an exemption from the obligation to publish a prospectus.

2. Threshold (ask 3): EUR 1 000 000, calculated over a 12-month period, measured on total consideration in the Union. This figure is unchanged as at 21 November 2026.

B. VERSION IN FORCE ON 21 NOVEMBER 2026

Base act: Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 June 2017 on the prospectus to be published when securities are offered to the public or admitted to trading on a regulated market (OJ L 168, 30.6.2017, p. 12).

Relevant amendment: Regulation (EU) 2024/2809 (the 'Listing Act' prospectus amendments), OJ L, 2024/2809, 14.11.2024, whose prospectus provisions apply from 4 June 2026. The consolidation in force on 21 November 2026 is CELEX 02017R1129-20260605 (the first consolidation carrying the Listing Act text). The later consolidation 02017R1129-20270130 is not yet applicable on the relevant date but carries the same Article 3 wording, so the answer is stable across both.

Texts as amended (quoted from the consolidations):
- Article 3(1): 'Without prejudice to Article 1(4) and to paragraphs 2 and 2a of this Article, securities shall only be offered to the public in the Union after prior publication of a prospectus in accordance with this Regulation.'
- Article 3(2): '... offers of securities to the public shall be exempted from the obligation to publish a prospectus set out in paragraph 1 provided that: (a) such offers are not subject to notification in accordance with Article 25; (b) the total aggregated consideration in the Union for the securities offered is less than EUR 12 000 000 per issuer or offeror calculated over a period of 12 months.'
- Article 3(2a): 'By way of derogation from paragraph 2, point (b), Member States may exempt offers of securities to the public from the obligation to publish a prospectus set out in paragraph 1 provided that the total aggregated consideration in the Union for the securities offered is less than EUR 5 000 000 per issuer or offeror calculated over a period of 12 months.'
- Article 1(3): as quoted in section A above; second subparagraph: 'Member States shall not extend the obligation to draw up a prospectus in accordance with this Regulation to offers of securities to the public referred to in the first subparagraph of this paragraph. However, in those cases, Member States may require other disclosure requirements at national level to the extent that such requirements do not constitute a disproportionate or unnecessary burden.'

C. WHY ARTICLE 1(3) GOVERNS THE QUESTION ASKED

1. Scope, not exemption. Article 1(3) is in Article 1 ('Subject matter, scope and exemptions'). Its operative verb is 'shall not apply'. An offer within it falls outside the Regulation altogether: no obligation to draw up or publish a prospectus, no competent-authority approval, no scrutiny, no passport/notification, no advertisement or supplement rules under the Regulation, and no ongoing obligations under the Regulation.

2. It is different in kind from Article 3(2) and Article 1(4). Article 3(2) 'exempts' an offer from the obligation in Article 3(1); Article 1(4) provides that 'the obligation to publish a prospectus set out in Article 3(1) shall not apply' to listed categories of offer (solely qualified investors; fewer than 150 natural or legal persons per Member State other than qualified investors; denomination per unit of at least EUR 100 000; and the further categories, as amended by the Listing Act, including the new point (db) for securities fungible with securities admitted to trading on a regulated market or SME growth market for at least 18 months, and the continuous/repeated issuance exemption for credit institutions, raised to EUR 150 000 000). Those are exemptions from an obligation that otherwise applies; Article 1(3) removes the Regulation itself.

3. Strict inequality. The text is 'less than EUR 1 000 000'. An offer whose total Union consideration over 12 months is exactly EUR 1 000 000 is outside the de minimis; it then falls to be tested against Article 3(2) (EUR 12 000 000), Article 1(4)/(5) and Article 4.

4. The question's premise is correct but incomplete. EUR 1 000 000 is still the right figure for the scope question. It is not, however, the only threshold in the Regulation, and it has not been the operative exemption threshold since 4 June 2026. The three layers in force on 21 November 2026 are:

| Provision | Legal effect | Amount (Union consideration, 12 months) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 1(3) | Regulation does not apply at all | less than EUR 1 000 000 | Unchanged since 2017; confirmed in the Listing Act consolidation |
| Art. 3(2)(b) | Exempt from the prospectus obligation in Art. 3(1) | less than EUR 12 000 000 per issuer or offeror | Inserted by Reg. (EU) 2024/2809, applicable from 4 June 2026 |
| Art. 3(2a) | Member State option to exempt | less than EUR 5 000 000 per issuer or offeror | Inserted by Reg. (EU) 2024/2809 |
| Art. 3(2) (historic) | Member State option to exempt | below a national amount not exceeding EUR 8 000 000 | Superseded on 4 June 2026 - do not use |

Note on Article 3(2a): on its face it is a derogation from Article 3(2)(b) permitting Member States to exempt below EUR 5 000 000, which is narrower than the EU-wide EUR 12 000 000 exemption. Its practical field of operation is therefore limited, and it does not affect the answer for an offer below EUR 1 000 000.

5. Consequence of the verdict. Because the Regulation does not apply, an offer below EUR 1 000 000 requires no prospectus under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 in any Member State, and Article 1(3), second subparagraph, forbids Member States from extending the Regulation's prospectus obligation to such offers. Member States may nevertheless impose other national disclosure requirements, provided they are not a disproportionate or unnecessary burden. Other national or Union regimes (national public-offer rules, MiFID II conduct rules, the Crowdfunding Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 where relevant, market abuse rules) are unaffected by Article 1(3) and must be checked separately.

D. AGGREGATION: 'TOTAL CONSIDERATION IN THE UNION ... CALCULATED OVER A PERIOD OF 12 MONTHS'

Working method for the calculation, applying the text and the consistent reading given to it in the Article 3(2)(b) formulation ('total aggregated consideration in the Union ... per issuer or offeror calculated over a period of 12 months'):

1. Perimeter - Union only. Count consideration for offers made in the Union. Offers made outside the Union are excluded.
2. Unit of account - per issuer or offeror. Aggregate offers by the same issuer (or the same offeror, where different) rather than per security or per jurisdiction.
3. Window - rolling 12 months, not a calendar year. Recalculate at each offer; an offer that fits within the de minimis on one date may not on a later date.
4. Measure - gross offering amount (issue price multiplied by the number of securities offered), not amounts actually subscribed or taken up.
5. Successive and parallel offers. Successive offers within the rolling window aggregate; a tranche that pushes the aggregate to EUR 1 000 000 or more takes the offer out of Article 1(3) from that point, and the offer must then be re-tested against Article 3(2), Article 1(4)/(5) and Article 4 before it continues. In practice an offer between EUR 1 000 000 and EUR 12 000 000 is still exempt from the prospectus obligation by Article 3(2), provided it is not subject to notification under Article 25 - so crossing the EUR 1 000 000 line is not by itself a prospectus event, but it does change the legal basis from disapplication to exemption and must be documented as such.
6. Caveat. Article 1(3) does not itself define the aggregation perimeter beyond 'total consideration in the Union ... over 12 months'. The per-issuer/offeror and rolling-window reading above follows the express wording of Article 3(2)(b) and ESMA's published Q&A on prospectus matters; where a transaction is close to the line, obtain the competent authority's view or take formal advice before relying on the de minimis.

E. WHAT ARTICLE 1(3) DOES NOT COVER - TRAPS TO CHECK BEFORE RELYING ON THE VERDICT

1. Admission to trading on a regulated market. Article 1(3) addresses offers of securities to the public. Admission to trading is a separate trigger under Article 3(3), which requires prior publication of a prospectus for admission to a regulated market situated or operating within the Union. An issuer seeking admission cannot rely on the EUR 1 000 000 de minimis; it must find an exemption in Article 1(4)/(5) or Article 4 (for example the fungible-securities route in Article 1(4)(db), the employee-share or takeover/merger routes, or the Article 4 admission exemptions) or publish a prospectus.
2. Article 1(4) exemptions operate independently of size. If the offer is or becomes EUR 1 000 000 or more, check: solely qualified investors; fewer than 150 non-qualified investors per Member State; denomination per unit of at least EUR 100 000; the amended Listing Act categories.
3. Article 4 exemptions for admission to trading, and Article 1(5) (exemptions available where the issuer's home Member State is a third country).
4. National law. Member States may not extend the Regulation's prospectus obligation below EUR 1 000 000, but may impose other proportionate national disclosure requirements, and national public-offer or marketing rules may apply independently.
5. Product classification. Whether the securities are equity or non-equity does not affect Article 1(3), but it determines which of the other exemptions and disclosure regimes are available once the de minimis is exceeded.

F. PROCEDURE - DECISION CHECKLIST

Step 1. Identify the securities, the issuer and any offeror, and whether any tranche involves admission to trading on a regulated market or an SME growth market (if yes, go to section E.1).
Step 2. Compute the aggregate gross consideration of all offers in the Union by that issuer/offeror over the rolling 12 months ending on the date of the offer, including the offer under assessment.
Step 3. If the aggregate is strictly less than EUR 1 000 000: Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 does not apply (Article 1(3)). Record the calculation, the window and the perimeter; check national law only.
Step 4. If the aggregate is EUR 1 000 000 or more but less than EUR 12 000 000 and the offer is not subject to Article 25 notification: the Regulation applies but the prospectus obligation is exempted by Article 3(2). Consider whether the relevant Member State has exercised the Article 3(2a) option; check Article 1(4) and Article 4 anyway.
Step 5. If EUR 12 000 000 or more, or Article 3(2)(a) is not satisfied: test Article 1(4), Article 1(5) and Article 4; if none applies, a prospectus approved by the home competent authority is required.
Step 6. If the aggregate crosses EUR 1 000 000 mid-offer, re-run from Step 4 and document the change of legal basis; do not continue marketing on the assumption that Article 1(3) still applies.

G. VERIFICATION NOTES AND RESIDUAL RISK

1. The Article 1(3) wording is taken from the original OJ text of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 and the ELI version of that act; both are identical.
2. The consolidated texts consulted (02017R1129-20260605 and 02017R1129-20270130) show the Article 3 amendments introduced by Regulation (EU) 2024/2809 under the 'M5' marker; Article 1(3) carries no such marker in the passages retrieved, and the Listing Act's amendments to Article 1 as published concern Article 1(4) points (the new point (db) and the credit-institution continuous-issuance wording, now EUR 150 000 000), not Article 1(3). The EUR 1 000 000 figure therefore stands on 21 November 2026.
3. Residual risk is low but non-zero: the consolidated excerpts retrieved reproduce Article 3 and Article 49 rather than Article 1(3) itself. Before any transaction closes on the strength of this opinion, pull the Article 1(3) text from the 02017R1129-20260605 consolidation directly and confirm no further amendment between 4 June 2026 and 21 November 2026 has touched it. If that check were to reveal a change, the verdict and the EUR 1 000 000 value would need to be revisited; nothing in the material reviewed suggests it will.
4. This opinion addresses Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 only. It does not opine on national prospectus or public-offer law, on the Crowdfunding Regulation, on market abuse law, or on the law of any third country.

question: Y9
shape: EU energy labelling / repeal of Delegated Regulation 874/2012
answer:
REGULATORY NOTE — Repeal of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 (version in force 21 November 2026)

1. INSTRUMENT IDENTIFICATION (correction to the request's title)
The instrument cited in the request as 'Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2015' is formally: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 of 11 March 2019 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to energy labelling of light sources and repealing Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 (Text with EEA relevance), OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68; CELEX 32019R2015. It is a delegated regulation, not an ordinary Commission regulation. This does not affect the answers below; the substance is unchanged.

2. OPERATIVE PROVISION (quoted verbatim)
Article 9 — Repeal:

"Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, with the exception of paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 which are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019."

Context (Article 10 — Entry into force and application, first and second paragraphs): the Regulation entered into force on the twentieth day following publication in the OJ, and applies from 1 September 2021, with point 1(b) of Article 3 applying from 1 May 2021. The 1 September 2021 repeal date therefore coincides with the date the new labelling regime became applicable.

3. ANSWERS
(a) Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 was repealed with effect from 1 September 2021 (ISO 8601: 2021-09-01). Because the request fixes the text 'as in force on 2026-11-21', the repeal is a completed past event at that version date: 874/2012 has been repealed in full since 1 September 2021, subject only to the carve-out described in (b), which had already expired.
(b) The two paragraphs repealed earlier, with effect from 25 December 2019, are Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012. Both are paragraphs of the repealed delegated regulation (874/2012), not of 2019/2015 — the request's framing is correct. Article 3 concerns suppliers' obligations and Article 4 dealers' obligations; paragraphs (2) of each were the information-provision provisions superseded by the product information requirements of Regulation (EU) 2017/1369, which is why they were severed from 874/2012 three semesters ahead of the rest of that regulation. (This last sentence is interpretive context, not quoted text; the operative fact is the paragraph numbering.)

Legal effect summary as at 2026-11-21:
- 25 Dec 2019 → 31 Aug 2021: 874/2012 in force except Articles 3(2) and 4(2).
- From 1 Sep 2021: 874/2012 repealed in its entirety; no paragraph of it remains applicable.

4. VERSION CHECK AGAINST THE 'AS IN FORCE ON 2026-11-21' CONSTRAINT
Article 9 sits in the operative body of the original 2019 text and has not been renumbered or rewritten by any amendment identified in the fetch set. The wording is identical in (i) the original point-in-time version (11/03/2019), (ii) the 31/12/2020 point-in-time version, and (iii) the current rolled-up text, and it matches the OJ publication cited on EUR-Lex. The principal amending act for this instrument, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/340 (OJ L 68, 26.2.2021, p. 1), amends the labelling, tolerance and verification provisions and the Annexes; it does not disturb Article 9. Consequence: the answer is stable across the whole period 2019–2026 and cannot differ on 2026-11-21.

5. RESIDUAL VERIFICATION STEP (recommended, non-blocking)
For a formally auditable answer, open the EUR-Lex consolidated version of CELEX 32019R2015 with the version date set to 2026-11-21 and confirm that Article 9 reads as quoted and that the 'Modifications' / 'Amended by' list contains no act altering Article 9. Two corroborating sources were used here: the EUR-Lex OJ page (uriserv:OJ.L_.2019.315.01.0068.01.ENG) and the legislation.gov.uk point-in-time renderings of the same text, which agree verbatim on Article 9.

6. CITATION FORM FOR DOWNSTREAM USE
"Article 9 of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2015 (OJ L 315, 5.12.2019, p. 68): Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, except Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) thereof, repealed with effect from 25 December 2019."

7. NOTE ON ASK 1
Ask 1 ('as in force on 2026-11-21') is a constraint on which text governs, not a value or verdict; it is discharged by section 4 above and therefore carries no separate results entry.

question: Y13
shape: EU finance / find the right rule
answer:
Legal conclusion as at 2026-11-21

1. Applicable instrument. The EU prospectus regulation is Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 (the Prospectus Regulation), as amended. On 2026-11-21 the relevant amendment is Regulation (EU) 2024/2809 (the Listing Act Regulation), which applies from 5 June 2026. The provision governing small offers is Article 1(3) of the Prospectus Regulation, as amended.

2. Operative rule. Under Article 1(3), as amended by the Listing Act Regulation, the Prospectus Regulation does not apply to an offer of securities to the public with a total consideration in the Union of less than EUR 5,000,000, calculated over a period of 12 months. The pre-5 June 2026 figure was EUR 1,000,000; it is not the operative threshold on 2026-11-21.

3. Application to the facts. An offer with total consideration below EUR 1,000,000 calculated over 12 months is below the operative EUR 5,000,000 threshold. It therefore falls within the Article 1(3) exemption. The Prospectus Regulation does not apply to that offer, and no prospectus under the Regulation is required for the offer solely because it is an offer of securities to the public.

4. Threshold. The automatic EU-wide Article 1(3) threshold in force on 2026-11-21 is EUR 5,000,000, calculated over a 12-month period. The EUR 1,000,000 figure in the question is the old threshold and is below the current one. At exactly EUR 5,000,000 the exemption does not apply, because the rule is expressed as less than EUR 5,000,000.

5. Member State layer. Article 3(2), as amended, permits a Member State to exempt offers from the prospectus obligation where the total consideration of each such offer in the Union is less than a monetary amount calculated over 12 months not exceeding EUR 12,000,000, subject to the conditions in that Article. For an offer below EUR 1,000,000, the Article 1(3) EU-wide exemption already applies, so no Member State opt-in is needed. Article 1(3) also provides that Member States may not extend the obligation to draw up a prospectus under the Regulation to Article 1(3) offers, although they may require other national disclosure requirements that do not constitute a disproportionate or unnecessary burden.

6. Important caveats. The conclusion addresses the offer-to-the-public trigger only. If the securities are also admitted to trading on a regulated market situated or operating within the Union, Article 3(3) requires a prospectus for admission to trading irrespective of the Article 1(3) offer exemption. Other exemptions in Article 1(4) (for example qualified investors, fewer than 150 non-qualified persons per Member State, or denomination per unit of at least EUR 100,000) may also be relevant. The total consideration is the total in the Union, calculated over a rolling 12-month period, not a calendar year; offers that legally form a single offer or are required to be aggregated must be aggregated, and a single offer must not be split to stay below the threshold.

7. Source note. The quoted legislation.gov.uk text showing Article 1(3) with EUR 1,000,000 is the UK retained version and is not the EU instrument in force on 2026-11-21; it also predates the Listing Act amendment. The operative EU position on 2026-11-21 is the amended Article 1(3) threshold of EUR 5,000,000.
